newsitem.title: UK: Dlr/mark pressured as sterling tumbles further.
newsitem.headline: Dlr/mark pressured as sterling tumbles further.

text.p: The dollar came under pressure in Europe, following sterling lower as profit-taking on the pound continued and the mark regained composure, traders said.
The U.S. currency fell below 1.83 marks, while the pound failed to hold above 3.0 marks and shed another three pfennigs.

"Profit-taking on sterling/mark and dollar/mark is the key feature, and there is room for more of a correction after the rallies they have both had," said Nick Shamin, currency analyst at ANZ Investment in London.
Simmering talk the Bundesbank might switch to a variable repo rate next month has put some life back into the mark, meanwhile.
At 1500 GMT the dollar was at 1.8290/8300 marks, down from 1.8470/80 in late European trading on Monday. It was little changed against the yen at 117.70/80 from 117.60/70.
Sterling/mark was at 2.9828/38, down from 3.0130/40, while sterling/dollar stood at $1.6306/12 from $1.6321/26.
Simmering talk the Bundesbank might switch to a variable repo rate soon have put some life back into the mark, meanwhile.

While German rates are not expected to rise any time soon, traders were caught unawares last week when the Bundesbank set fixed rate repo tenders at 3.00 percent for just two weeks during its four-week summer recess.
Helped by short-covering after its recent decline, the German unit looked poised for a broader upwards correction, analysts said.

Claudio Demolli, foreign exchange analyst at Merrill Lynch in London, said nervousness will dominate the market in the run-up to August 12, when the Bundesbank invites bids from the money market for a new repo allocation at its regular tender.

"A repo rate increase is still not our baseline scenario and while a dollar bullish strategy is still our preferred long-term view, the extent of mark underweight exposure poses a considerable risk of a short-term correction," Demolli said.

Adding to a more hesitant dollar tone in the short term are growing expectations that the U.S. central bank is not about to raise the target Fed funds rate. This view intensified after Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey Hawkins testimony last week.

The second quarter employment cost index did nothing to change that view as it was in line with expectations, showing growth of 0.8 percent. The index of U.S. consumer confidence fell to 126.5 in July, down more than three points from June's revised 129.9 but the data had little net impact, traders said.

The active market was the Dutch guilder, which fell to its lowest in almost four years against the mark, sparking speculation that the central bank will have to raise its key money market rate to stem the currency's slide.
The guilder fell below its central parity rate against the mark in the European exchange rate mechanism.

The guilder dropped to 1.126925 per mark in European trade, its lowest since August 1993, from 1.126675/6750 late in Europe on Monday. It last traded at 1.126850/6950. - Astrid Zweynert London newsroom + 44 171 542 7792
